analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only (docs/reference/configuration.md and docs/reference/model-registry-format.md). No executable code was changed. Reviewed the head text of configuration.md lines 481-715 and the model-registry-format.md patch and base text.

One security-relevant documented change is the new DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE (~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json). It appears in the patch excerpt, not in the numbered head units I received. It describes an owner-only cache of fully verified managed-load weight hashes, each bound to every file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. Startup registration reuses a matching record instead of re-hashing. This touches T-012 (operator replaces weights), T-027 (weight substitution) and A-004. An operator with write access could in principle edit the record or replace a file while preserving the metadata. That is a source-side question, not a documentation regression, because the implementation (VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift) was not supplied. The integration pass should check that the record is integrity-protected or rebound to the current file state. It should also check that pre/post-load verification still runs and that the coordinator weight_hash check is not weakened. The doc says fresh pre/post-load verification retains its rules, but that claim is unverified here.

The model-registry-format.md change documents PageCache.drop after hashing. This is a memory and availability behavior and does not change what is verified. configuration.md line 584-590 documents F_NOCACHE reading plus a page-cache drop and a managed GLM load publishing its own per-file SHA-256 verification. The text says this publishes verification instead of bracketing passes. That is a verification-flow change worth checking in source, but no concrete evidence of a weakened control is present in the docs.

The SSD prefix cache controls (lines 615-647) are consistent with T-041: the 1800s TTL cap, the DEBUG-only key file, and the ephemeral fallback gating. No new exposure is evident. No findings; source-level checks of VerifiedWeightHashStore and the GLM verification publication are recommended.
